relationships.subject: PAR2
relationships.evidence_quote: The mechanism of the pronociceptive effect induced by PAR2 stimulation involves the activation of spinal protein kinases and TRPV1 receptors.

relationships.subject: SB 366791
relationships.evidence_quote: Intrathecal PAR2-activating peptide (AP) administration aggravated the carrageenan-induced thermal hyperalgesia, and this was prevented by a TRPV1 antagonist (SB 366791)

relationships.subject: FSLLRY-NH2
relationships.evidence_quote: Importantly, the carrageenan-induced hypersensitivity was improved by the inhibition of spinal PAR2 using an i.t. treatment with PAR2 antagonist FSLLRY-NH2.

relationships.subject: PAR2
relationships.evidence_quote: Our findings clearly demonstrate that spinal PAR2 are already activated during the carrageenan-induced peripheral inflammation and enhance the nociceptive excitatory synaptic transmission in the spinal cord and contribute to thermal hyperalgesia.

key_findings: Spinal PAR2 activation aggravates carrageenan hyperalgesia and enhances mEPSC/sEPSC/eEPSC in dorsal horn neurons via TRPV1 and protein kinases.
PAR2 antagonist reduces hyperalgesia and EPSCs, indicating constitutive spinal PAR2 activation in inflammation.
